pageCache.text:
Trust, Friendship, Courage, Respect
Dunbury
Dunbury Academy is a very special place. We are a small primary school, serving the villages of the Winterborne Stickland, Winterborne Whitechurch, Winterborne Kingston, Milton Abbas and the surrounding area. Our community of villages come together at our school and are untied through our shared vision and values, just like the trees come and stand together on Dunbury Hill in our window emblem.
Useful Links
Latest News
Follow Us
Look out for our Dunbury CE Primary Academy Y6 pupils in the Echo!
Three of our pupils were privileged to attend the royal visit in Blandford today, representing Dunbury CE Primary Academy in the Blandford Schools Network. Between us, we got to shake hands with Their Majesties and have a little chat! It was a truly memorable occasion and the town looked spectacular. Thank you for all the hard work that went into it.
Some cool, shady activities today in the Purbecks: a visit to Corfe Castle and a blindfolded obstacle course! What a wonderful adventure - Year 4 will sleep well tomorrow night!
Y4 have had a lovely first day on residential. They enjoyed their dinner this evening and even sent their compliments to the chef. This evening we have had a lovely activity - we won't tell you too much as we don't want to spoil it for them. We look forward to our visit to Corfe Castle tomorrow. Mrs De Bardi and Mrs Duerdoth :) :)
We can't let the week end without thanking our fabulous Friends of Dunbury Academy for putting on a fantastic summer fair on Saturday! We are very lucky to have such supportive families, all pulling together to raise funds to enrich the children's school experience. It really was a cracker! Special thanks also to the amazing Dorset Police Cadets who volunteered on stalls and helped set up and pack down - your generous support was much appreciated.
Year 6 are having a whale of a time on their well- earned residential camping trip! Who doesn't love a spot of light archery and axe-throwing before dinner?! They are being a true credit to the school, living our Dunbury CE Primary Academy values of trust, respect, courage and friendship. They are a pleasure to be having fun with!
The children asked....and the Dunbury CE Primary Academy School Council delivered! Here they are leading a super assembly to the rest of the school, introducing the play equipment that was voted for. Pupil voice at its best
Year 3 and 4 are fantastic on the ukelele! Today's little tune was Ho- Hey by the Lumineers - they nailed it!
Our wonderful Mental Health in Schools team are running a webinar this Thursday 7th May to support any parents who would like help or information about supporting anxiety in children aged 11 years and under. We hope you find it helpful: https://events.teams.microsoft.com/event/ecd3294a-7fd9-4078-8607-1618037c6999@37c354b2-85b0-47f5-b222-07b48d774ee3
We highly recommend this Teams session for some really powerful, supportive information on healthy (and unhealthy) children's digital use.The registration link is in the comments- see you there!
A wonderful World Book Day at Dunbury CE Primary Academy and Dunbury Academy Early Years!! Dressing in character, visiting a book fair, reading with buddies, writing stories, listening to stories read by our wonderful community members in Winterborne Whitechurch village hall and a visiting theatre company telling us fearsome stories of olde!
We are hiring! Our children need a midday supervisor to help them have safe and happy lunchtimes. Do you love working with children and want to be part of a friendly community with high expectations that bring out the best in every child? We want to meet you! We have a lovely, welcoming staff team in a school operating across two bases in the beautiful rural settings of Winterborne Whitechurch and Winterborne Kingston. Want to know more? Here's how to apply! https://mynewterm.com/jobs/140561/EDV-2026-DCEA-17489
Dunbury CE Primary Academy would love you to post your blue Tesco tokens to help raise money for our outdoor gazebo! The children really need a quiet outdoor space that can be used for play or learning in all weathers- please support us! Tesco Stronger Starts is open until 31 March.

Governors
Dunbury Church of England Academy Standards and Ethos Committee
Who is the Academy Standards and Ethos Committee (ASEC)?
The Academy Standards and Ethos Committee (ASEC) is a voluntary group of Governors who carry out many of the functions of a Governing Body. The Governors report to an overarching body called the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust Board. The Governors are responsible for the strategic direction of Dunbury C of E Academy and monitor the impact and implementation of the Academy Improvement Plan by holding the school to account for its actions. In this respect, the Governors work alongside the Headteacher and are a key part of Dunbury’s Leadership Team.
Together with the school the Governors will promote high achievement in all curriculum areas so that children can accomplish the very best in all they do, in a safe and caring environment.
What do we do?
The Academy Standards and Ethos Committee are bound by a Scheme of Delegation, Constitution and Terms of Reference. These documents provide the set of rules by which the Governors abide in supporting the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust Board (DSAT) take responsibility for Dunbury C of E Academy.
More information about DSAT and the Governor role can be found on the governance section of the DSAT Website We are members of the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust and the governance of the Trust belongs to the main DSAT Board. Our Scheme of Delegation also includes our Constitution and Terms of Reference. Paper copies can be obtained through the school office or by using the contact us option on this website. You can find details of the Trust Board and details of our Trust Governance by visiting the Trustees page,
Governor Membership
Governor Meeting Attendance
The Chair of the Academy Standards and Ethos Committee for Dunbury is Tracey Hughes and can be contacted by email at trhughes@dunbury.dsat.org.uk. A copy of ASEC meeting minutes can be made available by request from the clerk, Tracy Ruffle, and can be contacted at truffle@dioceseofsalisbury.onmicrosoft.com

pageCache.text:
Home Learning
All remote learning can be found on Teams. Please log on using your child's log in details, provided to you by the teachers before Christmas. If you have misplaced these details, please contact your class teacher on email or the office.
Below, you will find a Step-By-Step Guide to using Teams for Remote Learning, as well as information about the remote learning that Dunbury are offering our children.
We recommend taking physical breaks away from the screen and table where the children are working, every hour.
Online resources for families
Here is a list of helpful resources which can be used as remote learning activities.
Reception, Year 1 and Year 2:
Oxford Owl - Practise your reading skills within the Read Write Inc section or the Oxford Reading Levels. Message your class teacher on Teams for your child's log in details.
Numbots - Practise your number bond skills and fluency in this robot-filled game. Message your class teacher on Teams for your child's log in details.
Hit The Button - Quick-fire maths practice of number bonds. No log-in necessary.
Times Tables Rock Stars - Practise your times tables skills, whilst collecting coins to buy guitars, outfits and crazy wigs! Message your class teacher on Teams for your child's log in details.
Read Theory - Practise your reading comprehension and fluency, whilst collecting Knowledge Points. Message your class teacher on Teams for your child's log in details.
Other useful resources to help support your child's learning
Letter formation chart - support your child to form their letters correctly. Click on the image to see a larger version.
Presentation Expectations - support your child to present their work to the same standard as they would in school. Click on the pencil to see a copy of the expectations for all year groups.
Maths Understanding - support your child in their maths understanding by watching some parent guide videos created by our teachers. Click on the image to navigate to the videos.

Saplings After School Club
We offer a safe, caring and fun environment for your child, after school for children aged 4 to 11 years on our Dunbury Primary site. Children from the Early Years site will be transported to the Primary site after school. The children are provided with a range of activities from exploring the school grounds to team games and crafts. We also recognise that some children prefer quieter activities and a chance to relax and have some down-time after school and so also provide colouring and reading as well as a big screen to watch. Children will enjoy healthy snack such as plain biscuits and fresh fruit or yoghurts alongside more substantial snacks such as toast. Please see the attached information for further details.

pageCache.pageTitle: Dunbury Church of England Academy  - Sports Premium

Sports Premium
From September 2013 the Government has given every primary school in England funding to be used to develop the teaching and learning in physical education and sport within schools. Within the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust we aim to provide high quality sport.
At Dunbury Academy, we believe that Physical Education (PE) is essential for children’s social, emotional, physical and mental wellbeing. It is our intension for all pupils to receive high-quality PE and learning opportunities that lead children achieving their personal best. We work towards encouraging children to make healthier lifestyle choices, develop key life skills and to show excellent sportsmanship. We aim for all children to be physically active for sustained periods during the school week. We also aspire for all children to swim at least 25 metres before leaving primary school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Dunbury Church of England Academy  - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Our Curriculum Intent
At Dunbury, we believe that is it the right of each new generation to be better than the preceding one. We want our children to become nurturing compassionate global citizens who can make complex decisions in intelligent ways.
Our vision is foundation of our curriculum and therefore the roots of the tree. It has its biblical underpinning in Galatians 3:28, “for we are all one in Christ”. Our knowledge tree comes from the strength of our vision, keeping us rooted in the aspiration we have for our pupils and community.
The trunk and branches of the tree represents the core of our culture which is based on our values. Our values drive and steer us in building our school community as one in which we thrive and flourish. They underpin our behaviours and attitudes towards ourselves and others. They are the guiding light that we return to when we feel uncertain or challenged.
Our curriculum drivers are the leaves that provide the tree with energy to grow the knowledge of the national curriculum. They feed the learning through developing curiosity, language and resilience for learning.
Our Vision: Strength in difference, together we are one, together we fly high
Our six curriculum themes linked to our vision aim to develop our children’s awareness about: themselves and others; our world and our role as its custodians; and collaboration and aspirations.
Strength in self
We aim to teach children about the importance of physical and mental health and the five ways to well-being. We want to develop an understanding of the character strengths needed to be resilient and successful and provide opportunities to reflect upon the ‘inner person’ and how this makes them wonderfully unique and valuable.
Strength in difference
We want our children to develop a curiosity about the diversity in our world and communities and through this develop a growing empathy, concern and compassion for how to treat others. This includes understanding the inequalities in our communities and how to be inclusive and bring about positive change to combat equality and equity.
Together in our communities
Having started to develop a ‘theory of mind’ (an understanding that others have minds like our own and so have different thoughts feelings and views), we want to equip our children with the knowledge and understanding needed to develop self-regulation, make friends and negotiate. We aim to provide opportunities for children to reflect upon how they can have an impact on others and how others can have an impact upon them.
Together in our world
We want our children to see themselves as custodians of our world and environment. We aim to do this through providing opportunities to explore our responses to the wonder of the natural world and human creativity and investigate the human impact on the natural environment, recognising cause and effect.
Be Heard
At Dunbury we want to develop every child’s unique voice through broadening their language, developing good listening skills and an understanding of how to treat others with kindness and respect. We want our children to be able to communicate in a variety of ways to get their message across powerfully and politely.
Be Aspirational
At Dunbury we want our children to grow and flourish as unique and curious individuals with the resilience and determination to continually challenge themselves, to innovate, to aspire and to achieve highly. We aim to teach them that achieving our goals takes time and practice and failed attempts along the way are opportunities to reflect and reset.
Our Christian Values
Our Christian Values
Our curriculum and vision is underpinned by our core Christian values of friendship, respect, courage and trust. Our values underpin everything we do and the behaviour that we aspire to achieve on a daily basis.
British Values
We promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.
Our Curriculum Drivers
When designing our curriculum, we took into account the needs of our learners and community, our vision and values, and the location of our school. These ‘big ideas’ or curriculum drivers are used to underpin the development work we undertake in all areas of school life and to ensure our curriculum offer is enriched and personalised to our children and their families.
Our Curriculum Maps
Our curriculum maps are the overview of how our curriculum drivers, vision, the national curriculum and the early years foundation stage are organised and connected throughout the school. As a small rural school with mixed age classes, we have laid out our curriculum on a rolling basis. As a child moves through the school they experience coverage of the curriculum through different topics. Beech and Maple follow the KS1 map, Cherry the Lower KS2 and Golden Willow and Scots Pine, Upper KS2
Please click on the links below to see our curriculum maps for this year.
EYFS Curriculum Map
Music tuition
We are fortunate to have very well-resourced music provision at Dunbury. In addition to this core curriculum, in Years Three and Four children embark on a programme of study with Dorset Music Service, studying an instrument which might be anything from the flute to the violin, from samba drums to trombones.
Children at Dunbury are offered the opportunity to learn to play an instrument through peripatetic tuition provided by the Dorset Music Service. If your child is interested in starting music lessons then please enquire for more details at the school office. Here is a link to the Dorset Music Service website where you can find information on instrument hire, funding opportunities, playing opportunities and much more:
www.dorsetmusicservice.org.uk
Please note, if you are in receipt of certain benefits or your child is eligible for free school meals, we will may be able to provide some support towards music tuition as part of our Pupil Premium strategy. Please speak to the office for details.
